sections.html: Males reach a maximum length of about 8 cm; females stay smaller, at only 6-7 cm.

Both sexes of the variety currently available have black bands in the vertical fins. Males can be recognized best by the overall shape (larger and more slender). In males the black vertical bands are more intense and the males have a bright red band in the dorsal fin, which is lacking in females. A female is also quite easy to recognize by its behaviour, as in Crenicichla compressiceps the females are the ones that wear the trousers.
